chapters.name: Basic Food Safety
chapters.summary: What foodborne illness is, its common symptoms, the people at higher risk, and the biological, chemical, and physical hazards that can make food unsafe.
keyPoints: Foodborne illness is a disease carried or passed to people by food.
Hazards are biological (germs), chemical (cleaners), and physical (glass, metal).
Young children, older adults, and people with weak immune systems are at higher risk.

chapters.name: Personal Hygiene
chapters.summary: How and when to wash your hands, how to use gloves, hand and nail care, work clothes, and which illnesses and symptoms you must report to your manager.
keyPoints: Handwashing takes at least 20 seconds; scrub for 10 to 15 seconds.
Change gloves when they are dirty or torn, between tasks, and after handling raw meat.
Report vomiting, diarrhea, jaundice, and a diagnosed foodborne illness to your manager.

chapters.name: Cross-contamination and Allergens
chapters.summary: How germs move from one food or surface to another, how to store and prepare food to prevent it, and how to keep major food allergens away from guests who cannot eat them.
keyPoints: Store ready-to-eat food above raw meat, seafood, and poultry.
Use separate equipment, or clean and sanitize between raw and ready-to-eat food.
The FDA lists nine major food allergens, including sesame.

chapters.name: Time and Temperature
chapters.summary: The temperature danger zone, how to use a thermometer, and how to receive, store, thaw, cook, hold, cool, and reheat food safely.
keyPoints: Cook poultry to 165°F, ground beef to 155°F, and whole cuts of beef, pork, and fish to 145°F.
Cool from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours, then to 41°F or lower within the next 4 hours.

chapters.name: Cleaning and Sanitation
chapters.summary: The difference between cleaning and sanitizing, how to set up and use a three-compartment sink, safe chemical storage, garbage handling, and signs of pests.
keyPoints: Cleaning removes dirt; sanitizing reduces germs to safe levels.
Three-compartment sink order: wash, rinse, sanitize, then air-dry.
Store chemicals away from and below food, in their labeled containers.
